title: 2020 AMC 12A 17
statement: The vertices of a quadrilateral lie on the graph of \(y = \ln x,\) and the \(x\)-coordinates of these vertices are consecutive positive integers. The area of the quadrilateral is \(\ln\dfrac{91}{90}.\) What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the leftmost vertex?

solutions.text:
Let the vertices have \(x\)-coordinates \(n, n+1, n+2, n+3\) with \(y\)-coordinates \(\ln\) of those values. Applying the shoelace formula and simplifying, the area is \(\ln\dfrac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)}.\)

Setting \(\dfrac{(n+1)(n+2)}{n(n+3)} = \dfrac{91}{90}\) gives \(1 + \dfrac{2}{n^2 + 3n} = \dfrac{91}{90},\) so \(n^2 + 3n = 180.\)

Then \((n - 12)(n + 15) = 0,\) so \(n = 12.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the \(x\)-coordinates be \(n, n+1, n+2, n+3\) and apply the shoelace formula
